```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
# Parameters
n <- sample(8:20, 1)
p <- sample(seq(0.10, 0.60, by = 0.05), 1)
x <- sample(1:(n-1), 1)

# Correct answer
correct <- round(dbinom(x, size = n, prob = p), 4)

# Plausible distractors
opt2 <- round(pbinom(x, size = n, prob = p), 4)     # P(X ≤ x)
opt3 <- round(1 - pbinom(x - 1, n, p), 4)           # P(X ≥ x)
opt4 <- round(dbinom(max(0, x - 1), n, p), 4)       # P(X = x-1)
opt5 <- round(dbinom(min(n, x + 1), n, p), 4)       # P(X = x+1)
opt6 <- round(1 - pbinom(x, n, p), 4)               # P(X > x)

options <- c(correct, opt2, opt3, opt4, opt5, opt6)

# Avoid duplicated options
while(length(unique(options)) < 6){
  n <- sample(8:20, 1)
  p <- sample(seq(0.10, 0.60, by = 0.05), 1)
  x <- sample(1:(n-1), 1)

  correct <- round(dbinom(x, size = n, prob = p), 4)
  opt2 <- round(pbinom(x, size = n, prob = p), 4)
  opt3 <- round(1 - pbinom(x - 1, n, p), 4)
  opt4 <- round(dbinom(max(0, x - 1), n, p), 4)
  opt5 <- round(dbinom(min(n, x + 1), n, p), 4)
  opt6 <- round(1 - pbinom(x, n, p), 4)

  options <- c(correct, opt2, opt3, opt4, opt5, opt6)
}
```

Question
========

A production process generates defective items with probability $p=`r p`$ independently from one item to another. Suppose that $n=`r n`$ items are inspected and let $X$ denote the number of defective items. What is the probability that **exactly $`r x`$ items are defective**?

Answerlist
----------

* `r sprintf("%.4f", correct)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt2)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt3)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt4)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt5)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt6)`

Solution
========

Since $X \sim Bin(n=`r n`, p=`r p`)$, the probability of observing exactly $`r x`$ defective items is

$$
P(X=`r x`)
=
\binom{`r n`}{`r x`}
(`r p`)^{`r x`}
(1-`r p`)^{`r n - x`}.
$$

Substituting the values,

$$
P(X=`r x`)
=
\binom{`r n`}{`r x`}
(`r p`)^{`r x`}
(1-`r p`)^{`r n - x`}
=
`r sprintf("%.4f", correct)`.
$$
